# Singapore Property & Finance - Daily Brief (property + finance)
_Auto-generated 21 Nov 2026 (SGT). Source-linked. General information only; exact figures and eligibility are confirmed case by case._

## Private Market: New Sales & Major Land Bids

- **October 2026 developer sales surge to 1,716 units** - Developers sold 1,716 new private homes (excluding ECs) in October 2026, a 479.7% jump from September's 296 units and the highest monthly volume since October 2025, led by Thomson Reserve and Lucerne Grand. [Source](https://www.99.co/singapore/insider/october-2026-developer-sales/)
- **CapitaLand-led consortium bids $1.824 billion for Jurong East white site** - The Town Hall Link site in Jurong Lake District could deliver around 1,200 new homes near the MRT if the bid is accepted. [Source](https://stackedhomes.com/1-8-billion-bid-turn-jurong/)
- **98% of Marina One Residences resellers recorded losses** - 45 of 46 resales at Marina One Residences in the 12 months to 18 October 2026 sold below the owner's purchase price, with a median loss of $339,000, compared to 5.2% of condo resales islandwide recording losses. [Source](https://stackedhomes.com/marina-one-residences-45-46-resales/)

## HDB Market: Million-Dollar Flats & Rentals

- **238 HDB flats sold at $1 million or more in October 2026** - That figure is up sharply from 86 million-dollar HDB transactions recorded a year ago, with Toa Payoh leading at 39 deals and Queenstown close behind at 31. [Source](https://stackedhomes.com/238-hdb-flats-sold-s1m-october/)
- **Condo rental volumes ease while HDB rents continue to climb** - Condo leasing activity slowed further in October 2026 while HDB rental volumes held steady, with the year-end holiday season expected to keep overall leasing activity subdued. [Source](https://www.99.co/singapore/insider/condo-rental-activity-slows-down-in-october-2026-as-hdb-rents-continue-to-climb/)

## Construction Costs & Supply Outlook

- **Rising construction costs may push developers toward renovation over new builds** - JLL expects Singapore construction costs to rise 2.5%–3.5% in 2026, a trend that could lead developers to favour asset enhancement and adaptive reuse rather than new development. [Source](https://stackedhomes.com/rising-construction-costs-set-force-developers/)
